Operational Risk Management
The Operational Risk Management team plays a key role in identifying, assessing, monitoring, and reporting operational risks across the bank. During your rotation, you will gain exposure to a broad range of operational risk activities and learn how to:

About the Role
Position Title   : AVP Internal Audit Risk Management
Corporate Title: Associate/Assistant Vice President, Internal Audit
Reporting to    : Director
Location          : MGS - Bengaluru
Shift Timings  : 1.30 PM to 10.30 PM IST

Job Profile
Position details / Job summary:
The Associate Auditor II role within the Internal Audit function is responsible for executing independent, objective assurance and consulting activities designed to assess and evaluate the effectiveness of the Bank’s governance, risk management and control processes.  It reports to either a VP, Audit Lead or a Director, Sr. Audit Lead.  This role includes, but is not limited to, execution of end-to-end audit process (e.g. planning, fieldwork testing, reporting, issues validation, etc.) and independently owning audit administration activities and project deliverables across the organization.

Roles and Responsibilities
- Maintain compliance with audit methodology, while also operating within industry best practices, applicable regulations, and internal and external professional practice expectations.
- Act as a leader and role model and continuously improve self and department.
- Build relationships with peers and clients within organization and exhibit a high standard of performance and professional conduct that will create a culture of integrity and inclusion; where all individual and departmental choices are rooted in good judgment and support MUFG's Ethics and Conduct Principles.
- Operate with an innovative and flexible mindset by continuously identifying ways to enhance consistency, efficiency, quality and/or value.
- Demonstrate professional skepticism and personal accountability.
- Lead walkthrough meetings and interviews with business stakeholders to develop understanding of business processes.
- Lead formal discussions with business stakeholders throughout the duration of audit engagements to communicate status or concerns.
- Identify potential risks and controls and assist in developing scope and work programs.
- Evaluate design and operational effectiveness of internal controls and identify control weaknesses.
- Generate insightful, meaningful observations that effectively convey significance and impact on risk and/or risk management practices, reporting findings and audit issues to Audit Management.
- Prepare workpapers and audit reports with documented results that adhere to methodology, applicable standards and regulatory requirements, using appropriate business and technical language.
- Document workpapers demonstrating the work was appropriately performed (e.g., detailed lead sheets describing the control attributes that were tested and the results were documented in a manner to support the conclusions reached, effectiveness and sustainable controls are evident in documentation). Documentation should stand alone to enable re-performance.
- Identify control weaknesses and escalate and discuss findings with Audit Management and business stakeholders as appropriate.
- Complete work on a timely basis and deliver work products that meet objectives and standards of methodology, applicable standards and regulatory requirements.

Education, Licensure, Year of Experience (and type of work experience):
- A Bachelor’s degree, preferably in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration or related business discipline at an accredited college or university.

Skills and Experience :
- Minimum of 5-6 years and/or equivalent of experience of internal audit and/or equivalent of experience with the financial services industry, related markets, and related regulatory agencies.
- Experience preferred in operational risk/corporate functions, specifically business continuity management, third party risk, change management, and/or human resources.
- Exhibits effective communication (both verbal and written), negotiation and presentation skills; strong interpersonal skills; and ability to engage with all levels of internal audit and business line management.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
- Employs critical thinking skills to identify pragmatic recommendations within an evolving and increasingly complex regulatory and risk management environment.
- Proficiency in technology as required for assigned areas (MS Office, audit data analytics, etc.).
- Ability to travel may be required.

Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG) is an equal opportunity employer. We view our employees as our key assets as they are fundamental to our long-term growth and success. MUFG is committed to hiring based on merit and organsational fit, regardless of race, religion or gender.

jobs.description:

Join MUFG, where being inspired is expected and making a meaningful impact is rewarded.

Overview
The role supports the Financial Risk function within MUFG Canada Risk Management, with a focus on the production, analysis, governance and continuous enhancement of liquidity risk, market risk, credit risk and interest rate risk in the banking book reporting. Reporting to the Financial Risk Vice President, the incumbent is responsible for preparing and maintaining recurring risk reports, supporting ECL and portfolio credit risk analysis, monitoring risk appetite and limit metrics, maintaining EUC and procedure documentation, and assisting with committee materials for IRC, ECC, Liquidity Risk and Market Risk governance forums. The role requires excellent technical capability, including advanced data analysis, Excel/Power Query/VBA automation, source-data reconciliation, AI literacy and the ability to responsibly leverage AI-enabled tools to improve reporting efficiency, data quality, trend analysis, control effectiveness and management insight. The incumbent must demonstrate strong knowledge of the underlying risk metrics, data sources such as OVS extracts, Bloomberg and internal reporting files, and the ability to translate complex technical outputs into clear, audit-ready commentary and management materials.

Key Accountabilities
Risk reporting, analytics and governance support - responsibilities include:
- Prepare, analyze and maintain recurring Financial Risk reports across liquidity risk, market risk, credit risk and IRRBB, including Liquidity Early Warning Indicators, Liquidity Limit Dashboard, Liquidity Stress Testing, daily and monthly liquidity monitoring, VaR, stress testing, DV01, sensitivity measures, portfolio concentration, IFRS 9 ECL, Watchlist inputs, Risk Appetite metrics and interest rate risk analytics.
- Compile and validate source data from OVS extracts, Bloomberg, internal risk files, Treasury reports, Middle Office data, Finance inputs, facility and commitment data, exposure reports and locally maintained EUC tools to support recurring production and independent review of risk metrics.
- Support the preparation of IRC, ECC, Liquidity Risk, Market Risk and other governance materials by compiling metrics, drafting commentary, preparing exhibits, explaining drivers, documenting assumptions and ensuring materials are accurate, complete and delivered within required timelines.
- Perform review and challenge of report outputs, investigate material movements or exceptions, document rationale, reconcile data back to source systems, and escalate breaches, data issues or control concerns in accordance with applicable procedures.

Support for stakeholders - responsibilities include:
- Coordinate with Treasury, Middle Office, Finance, Operations, Compliance, business lines, regional risk teams and Head Office to obtain data, validate assumptions, clarify methodology, and support timely completion of Financial Risk deliverables.
- Provide support, oversight and guidance to first line and independent risk monitoring functions on risk reporting, risk appetite monitoring, limit usage, breach escalation and remediation tracking.
- Support audit, regulatory and internal review requests by maintaining clear evidence, audit trails, version logs, approvals and supporting documentation for recurring reporting processes.

- Monitor relevant regulatory, Head Office and regional risk requirements and assist in translating them into local policies, procedures, controls, testing approaches and reporting processes.
- Support the review and enhancement of local risk policies, procedures, EUC documentation and user manuals, including documentation for EWI, liquidity limits, LST, market risk reporting, RFR-linked submissions and ECL processes.
- Assist with annual recalibration and methodology review processes for liquidity risk metrics, EWI thresholds, LST assumptions, local limits and other Financial Risk measures, including coordination with ALRMO, Head Office and first line stakeholders.
- Identify opportunities to automate, streamline and strengthen recurring reports, tracking logs, confirmations and control processes while maintaining appropriate governance, documentation and change management.

Technical Skills
- Excellent technical skills, including advanced Microsoft Excel capability with complex formulas, Power Query, pivot tables, data validation, reconciliations, financial modelling, VBA/macros and automation techniques used to streamline recurring risk reporting processes.
- Strong knowledge of liquidity risk metrics and reporting, including Early Warning Indicators, Liquidity Stress Testing, liquidity limits, limit utilization, funds position, cash-flow analysis, contingency funding plan inputs, liquidity risk appetite measures, threshold recalibration and breach/escalation monitoring.
- Strong knowledge of market risk metrics and analytics, including VaR, stress testing, DV01, sensitivity analysis, limit monitoring, market data validation, rate and spread movements, exposure drivers and recurring market risk reporting packages.
- Strong knowledge of credit risk and ECL analytics, including IFRS 9 ECL, exposure and commitment utilization, portfolio concentration, industry and obligor analysis, facility data, credit exposure trends and credit risk appetite reporting.
- Working knowledge of IRRBB concepts and tools, including interest rate sensitivity, earnings and economic value perspectives, repricing profile analysis, scenario-based impacts, assumptions review and coordination with regional or Head Office stakeholders on IRRBB methodology and tool development.
- Ability to source, extract, reconcile and analyze data from multiple internal and external risk systems, Treasury and Middle Office files, Finance inputs, facility and commitment reports, shared-drive repositories, SharePoint sites and locally maintained EUC tools.
- Advanced data analytics capability, including the ability to work with large and complex data sets, identify data quality issues, perform variance and trend analysis, reconcile outputs across systems, design repeatable controls, and convert raw data into meaningful risk insights and executive-level commentary.
- Practical knowledge of AI-enabled productivity and analytics tools, with the ability to responsibly leverage AI to support data validation, report drafting, process documentation, variance investigation, coding assistance, workflow automation, knowledge management and management reporting, while maintaining appropriate human review, confidentiality and control standards.
- Ability to identify and implement opportunities for automation, AI-assisted analysis and process improvement in recurring reports, EUC tools, tracking logs, confirmations, procedure manuals, management materials and control evidence repositories.
- Experience preparing high-quality committee, management and audit materials, including metric dashboards, variance explanations, trend summaries, breach or exception commentary, methodology notes, procedure documentation and evidence packages.
- Sound understanding of financial risk concepts, governance expectations and control requirements, including liquidity risk, market risk, credit risk, IFRS 9 ECL, IRRBB, risk appetite metrics, stress testing, concentration risk, EUC governance and risk measurement methodologies.

Experience & Abilities
- Minimum of 3 years of banking, risk management, treasury, finance, audit, data analytics or related financial services experience; experience in a second line risk management function is preferred.
- Demonstrated ability to prepare, analyze and explain recurring risk reports and supporting materials across liquidity risk, market risk, credit risk and IRRBB, including EWI, LST, liquidity limits, VaR, stress testing, DV01, sensitivity measures, ECL, commitment utilization, concentration, risk appetite and governance reporting.
- Strong technical aptitude and curiosity, with a proven ability to learn new systems, adopt emerging technologies, use AI-enabled tools responsibly, and translate technical outputs into practical risk management conclusions.
- Strong analytical, investigative and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify data issues, explain key drivers, assess materiality, reconcile outputs to source data, validate AI-assisted outputs and recommend practical control or reporting improvements.
- Effective written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to draft concise commentary, document rationale, present results, and coordinate deliverables with stakeholders at different levels.
- Ability to manage multiple recurring deadlines, maintain strong attention to detail, preserve accurate audit trails, and ensure technology-enabled improvements remain transparent, controlled and well documented.

Education & Training
- University degree in finance, economics, mathematics, accounting, business, risk management, data analytics, computer science, information systems or a related discipline.
- Post-graduate education, professional designation or progress toward a designation such as FRM, CFA, CPA, MBA, data analytics certification, AI-related training or equivalent risk/finance certification is considered beneficial.
- Additional training in liquidity risk, market risk, credit risk, IFRS 9, regulatory reporting, data analytics, automation, responsible AI use, prompt engineering, model/EUC governance or technology risk controls is considered an asset.

The job description and related application pertains to an opportunity with either MUFG Bank, Ltd., Canada Branch (“MUFG Bank Canada”) or MUFG Securities (Canada), Ltd. (“MUFG Securities Canada”). The job description relates to the general nature, scope, quantity and quality of work contemplated for the position. Other duties and responsibilities not specifically described may be assigned from time to time, consistent with knowledge, skills and abilities of the incumbent. The receipt of an application by either MUFG Bank Canada or MUFG Securities Canada, as applicable, does not imply or guarantee employment.

2027 ARM Summer Analyst Program Overview: (6/7/2027 ~ 8/13/2027)

The Risk Management Summer Analyst Program at MUFG is designed to help you learn how the Bank maintains a disciplined approach to identifying, assessing, managing, reporting, and mitigating risks.

Our 10-week Summer Analyst Program begins in early June and is structured to provide rising seniors with hands-on experience and business exposure in the world of Risk Management. You will be placed in a specific group that allows you to concentrate and quickly develop the skills and knowledge required to become an integral part of the team. You will work alongside MUFG professionals at all levels who will serve as your instructors and mentors. Interns also have the opportunity to attend learning sessions led by Americas Risk Management professionals in all of the Risk Disciplines at the bank. The Risk Program is designed to help you experience just what it’s like to manage risk within a Global Investment Bank.

In this role, the Analyst will have opportunities to interact with colleagues within Americas Risk Management and the Lines of Business and Products Owners while rotating through activities in their assigned area of a given risk discipline.  With the goal of learning the components of the MUFG Risk Framework and how it is implemented within the Bank to effectively assess, monitor, and control risk.  Additionally, the Analyst will have the opportunity to work on cross functional projects to gain insights into how the various risk frameworks intersect and support the overall management of risk at the Bank and support the strategic goals of MUFG.

Based on background, interest, and firm need – interns will be selected to work in one of the following areas:
- Credit Risk Reporting: The reporting around risk of loss and reduction in capital, and weakened financial resiliency, arising from borrowers or counterparties not paying as agreed on loans or other contractual agreements.
- Liquidity Risk: The risk that the enterprise will not have, or may simply be perceived as not having, enough cash, liquid assets, or fulfill liabilities to fund loans, pay operating expenses, or other contractual obligations as they come due.
- Interest Rate Risk: T he risk that focuses on assessing how changes in market interest rates may affect the bank’s earnings and financial position.
- Operational Risk: The risk from events which may have an adverse effect on current projected financial condition and resilience arising from inadequate or failed internal processes or systems, human error or misconduct, or adverse external events.
- Enterprise Risk Management: Risks resulting from Strategic events. Additionally, encompassing Risk Governance functions such as risk appetite and risk reporting, etc.
- Quantitative Risk Control: The use of any Models invariably presents Model Risk, which is the potential for adverse consequences (e.g., financial loss, poor business and strategic decision-making, or damage to an organization’s brand) from decisions based on incorrect or misused Model outputs and reports.

Support & Guidance
Your assigned mentor/manager will provide goals and professional development guidance and conduct performance reviews as a commitment to our summer Analysts. You will also have the opportunity to network with employees across different business groups and at all levels of the organization. In our open and inclusive environment, senior colleagues will know who you are and will see the work you do. You will leave with a better understanding of the world of risk management.

At the end of the program, the opportunity exists to receive an offer for full time employment upon graduation. 80% Business Development & Relationship Management

- Identify and originate new treasury management opportunities through close partnership with Relationship Managers, Product, and other internal stakeholders.
- Deepen existing client relationships by understanding business objectives, cash flow dynamics, liquidity needs, and operational challenges, and delivering tailored treasury solutions.
- Leverage MUFG’s lending relationships, balance sheet, and broader product capabilities to expand wallet share and drive cross-sell opportunities.
- Participate in client account planning and strategic reviews, developing actionable growth plans based on client priorities, competitive positioning, and revenue opportunities.
- Lead treasury solution discussions with clients and prospects, including proposal development, solution design, pricing strategy, and contract negotiations.
- Maintain an active sales pipeline, deliver accurate forecasting, and provide regular reporting on business development activities and revenue generation.
- Partner with Product Management to provide client feedback, enhance existing capabilities, and identify emerging treasury solutions for the Financial Institutions sector.
- Prepare and present exception pricing and business cases to appropriate governance forums when required.
- Maintain detailed client records, deal activity, and competitive intelligence within bank’s sales management platforms.

20% Risk Management & Compliance
- Ensure all client activities and sales practices comply with applicable bank policies, regulatory requirements, and internal risk management standards.
- Maintain a strong understanding of KYC, AML, BSA, sanctions, and other regulatory requirements impacting financial institution clients.
- Support account onboarding activities and periodic client reviews by partnering with Compliance, Operations, and Coverage teams to ensure timely completion of required documentation and due diligence.
- Identify, escalate, and appropriately manage potential risks, suspicious activity, or compliance concerns in accordance with bank policy.
- Complete all required compliance, risk, and regulatory training and adhere to established control frameworks.
- Develop a thorough understanding of client business models, anticipated transaction activity, and treasury operating practices to support effective risk management and ongoing client monitoring.

The ideal candidate will have:
- 7–10 years of sales and relationship management experience, preferably with a leading transaction banking provider (domestic or international).
- Experience selling treasury products, liquidity, and commercial card solutions to insurance companies, asset managers, private equity funds, fund administrators, and other non-bank financial institutions.
- Provide strategic insights and thought leadership to clients.
- Established network and industry relationships within the Financial Institutions Group sector preferred
- Strong understanding of fund structures, capital call and distribution processes, subscription and redemption cash flows, fund administrator operating models, and insurance company balance sheet and liquidity management.
- Knowledge of the regulatory and operational considerations impacting financial institutions, including insurance companies, asset managers, private equity funds, and other non-bank financial institutions.
- Deep expertise in domestic and international payments, including a strong understanding of SWIFT messaging standards and payments infrastructure.
- Proven ability to identify, develop, negotiate, and close complex sales opportunities while building long-term client relationships.
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to effectively present and position the bank's solutions to sophisticated financial institution clients.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, and PowerPoint) and the responsible use of AI-enabled tools within the bank's risk and compliance framework.
- Willingness and ability to travel locally and regionally to meet with clients and prospects.

The Division Risk Manager (DRM) is a member of the First Line of Defense (FLoD) responsible for overseeing the identification, assessment, monitoring, and remediation of risks and issues within the assigned business unit. The role ensures effective execution of the Risk & Control Self-Assessment (RCSA) and Issue Management programs in alignment with enterprise standards and regulatory expectations.

The DRM is part of a team of approximately 4-5 risk managers responsible for day-to-day execution of risk and issue management activities and serves as a trusted risk advisor to business leadership.

Key Responsibilities
Risk & Control Self-Assessment (RCSA)
• Lead and execute the RCSA lifecycle in accordance with enterprise standards.
• Ensure comprehensive identification and assessment of Operational, Compliance, Third Party, Information, and Model Risks.
• Provide effective challenge to business stakeholders on risk identification, control design, and control effectiveness.
• Ensure risks, controls, and processes are accurately documented and maintained within OpenPages.
• Identify emerging risks and thematic control issues and escalate as appropriate.

Issue Management
• Serve as FLoD owner for Issue Management activities from identification through remediation and closure.
• Ensure timely identification, escalation, and documentation of issues where risk exceeds tolerance.
• Oversee root cause analysis, management action plans, remediation timelines, and remediation evidence quality.
• Govern issue changes, extensions, and escalation processes.
• Ensure remediation is completed in a timely, sustainable manner and is prepared for independent validation.

Qualifications
• 3-5 years of experience in operational risk management, audit, compliance, bank operations or related disciplines.
• Experience implementing, executing, building, or enhancing risk and control frameworks.
• Experience interacting with regulators on examinations and issue remediation.
• Experience partnering with Second Line of Defense (SLoD) and Third Line of Defense (TLoD) teams across issue lifecycles, examinations, and emerging risk identification.
• Experience presenting balanced risk perspectives to senior risk and control governance committees.
• Experience with process documentation (MS Visio), risk and control assessments, and issue validation.
• Excellent skills in risk assessment, governance, and reporting with strong understanding of business operations and financial markets preferred.
• Strong knowledge of inherent risks within the applicable business lines.
• Ability to analyze risk trends and identify indicators of changing risk levels.
• Ability to translate technical risk concepts into clear, business-oriented language.
• Demonstrated problem-solving skills with the ability to deliver innovative solutions with or without technology.
• Demonstrated experience working within a First Line of Defense model in a regulated financial institution.
• Experience with risk management systems such as OpenPages preferred.

Core Competencies
• Risk judgment and critical thinking
• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to tailor messaging to technical, business, and executive audiences
• Stakeholder engagement and influence
• Governance and escalation management
• Continuous improvement mindset

Education
• Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree preferred.

As organizations increasingly leverage artificial intelligence to drive innovation, improve customer experiences, enhance decision-making, and automate business processes, trusted and well-governed data has become foundational to managing AI risk. This role will serve as a key partner to business, technology, risk, compliance, model risk, legal, and governance teams to ensure that data supporting AI solutions is appropriately governed, controlled, transparent, and fit for purpose.
The successful candidate will combine expertise in data management, governance, controls, and risk management to help establish a scalable framework for identifying, assessing, monitoring, and mitigating AI-related data risks across the enterprise.
This is a senior individual contributor and team lead role with responsibility for influencing enterprise AI governance practices, supporting strategic AI initiatives, and helping drive responsible AI adoption throughout the organization.

AI Data Risk Management

- Help establish governance processes that promote the quality, integrity, transparency, lineage, and appropriate use of data throughout the AI lifecycle.

- Evaluate whether data used in AI solutions is adequately documented, understood, governed, and monitored.

Data Management & Accountability
- Drive accountability for data used within AI solutions and AI-enabled business processes.

- Improve transparency into how data supporting AI solutions is collected, transformed, governed, consumed, and monitored.

- Help establish ownership and stewardship models for AI-related data assets.

- Support management of critical data elements, business glossaries, data lineage, data quality controls, and AI-related inventories.

- Partner with business teams to improve the availability and trustworthiness of data supporting AI initiatives.

Risk & Regulatory Support
- Collaborate with Risk, Compliance, Legal, Privacy, and Audit teams to support evolving regulatory and governance expectations related to AI.

- Help identify opportunities to strengthen oversight and reduce AI-related operational, compliance, and reputational risks.

Stakeholder Leadership
- Act as a trusted advisor to senior leaders on AI-related data risks and governance considerations.

- Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.

- Demonstrated leadership experience through people management or leadership of significant cross-functional initiatives.

- Knowledge of AI governance, responsible AI principles, or emerging AI regulatory expectations.

- Experience with data catalogs, data quality platforms, workflow tools, lineage solutions, or governance technologies.

- Familiarity with model risk management, privacy programs, operational risk frameworks, or technology risk management.

- Experience within a banking, financial services, or highly regulated environment.

Job Summary:

We are seeking a highly motivated Analyst to join the Collateral Management Group ("CMG") within the Portfolio Management Group supporting the Commodity Finance business. The Analyst will be responsible for assisting with the administration, monitoring, and risk management of a portfolio of commodity finance credit facilities, including borrowing base facilities, transactional trade finance structures, and agency transactions.

The role serves as a key control function supporting transaction execution, collateral monitoring, borrowing base analysis, client servicing, and risk oversight. The successful candidate will work closely with Relationship Managers, Portfolio Managers, Operations, Credit, and borrowers to ensure financing activities are executed accurately, collateral is appropriately monitored, and emerging risks are promptly identified and escalated.

This position provides excellent exposure to commodity finance, asset-based lending, trade finance products, collateral structures, and credit risk management within a leading global financial institution.

Responsibilities:

Collateral Monitoring & Risk Analysis

- Review and analyze borrowing base reports, inventory reports, collateral schedules, accounts receivable aging reports, and other collateral-related information.

- Monitor client positions against approved borrowing base availability, credit limits, and facility sub-limits.

- Verify collateral eligibility, advance rate calculations, concentration limits, and compliance with approved credit parameters.

- Review mark-to-market reports, commodity pricing information, and position reports to identify emerging risks and trends.

- Assess the adequacy of collateral coverage and identify exceptions, discrepancies, or deterioration in risk profile.

- Escalate collateral deficiencies, reporting exceptions, and adverse developments to management and relevant stakeholders in a timely manner.

Transaction Execution & Facility Administration

- Support day-to-day financing activities, including loans, letters of credit, receivable purchases, payments, and other trade finance transactions.

- Review transaction requests to ensure consistency with approved credit structures and facility documentation.

- Coordinate with Operations, Relationship Management, and Portfolio Management teams to facilitate timely transaction execution.

- Monitor transaction processing timelines and proactively resolve execution issues or delays.

- Maintain accurate documentation, transaction records, and internal tracking tools.

Deal Support & Documentation Review

- Assist with the review of term sheets, credit approvals, legal documentation, amendments, and facility structures.

- Participate in transaction discussions relating to new business opportunities, amendments, and renewals.

- Develop an understanding of transaction mechanics, operational requirements, and collateral structures.

- Support facility closings and implementation of new transactions.

- Assist in identifying operational considerations and execution risks associated with new structures.

Agency Facility Management

- Support the administration of syndicated and agency-managed facilities.

- Monitor facility utilization, lender commitments, sub-limits, and borrower requests.

- Coordinate with lenders, borrowers, and internal teams regarding facility-related activities.

- Assist with letter of credit reconciliation and agency reporting requirements.

- Support responses to lender and borrower inquiries.

Client & Stakeholder Engagement

- Serve as a day-to-day point of contact for clients and internal stakeholders on operational and collateral-related matters.

- Build and maintain effective working relationships with Relationship Managers, Portfolio Managers, Operations, Credit, Legal, Compliance, and borrowers.

- Communicate facility updates, collateral developments, transaction status, and issue resolution in a timely and professional manner.

- Support a solutions-oriented approach while maintaining adherence to approved credit and risk parameters.

Controls, Compliance & Risk Management

- Maintain strong adherence to internal policies, credit approvals, procedures, and regulatory requirements.

- Perform control checks to ensure consistency between transaction activity, collateral reporting, and internal systems.

- Identify operational risks, control deficiencies, or process gaps and escalate appropriately.

- Maintain awareness of BSA/AML, OFAC, sanctions, and financial crime requirements applicable to assigned responsibilities.

- Demonstrate ownership and accountability for risk management activities within assigned portfolio responsibilities.

Skills & Experience:

- Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration, or a related discipline.

- 1–3 years of relevant experience within commercial banking, corporate banking, trade finance, credit, lending operations, treasury, or a related financial services environment.

- Strong analytical and quantitative skills with the ability to interpret financial, collateral, and transactional information.

- Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail.

- Strong verbal and written communication skills.

- Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

- Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and Microsoft Office applications.

Preferred Qualifications:
- Prior exposure to commodity finance, asset-based lending, collateral management, trade finance, supply chain finance, or structured lending.

- Familiarity with borrowing base facilities, inventory financing, receivables financing, and trade finance products.

- Working knowledge of banking platforms such as ACBS, LoanIQ, Trade360, or similar systems.

- Understanding of credit documentation, collateral structures, and operational transaction workflows.

- Experience reviewing client reporting packages, collateral certificates, position reports, or mark-to-market reports.

Join MUFG, where being inspired is expected and making a meaningful impact is rewarded.

OVERVIEW OF THE DEPARTMENT/SECTION
Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (“MUFG”) is one of the world’s leading financial groups. Headquartered in Tokyo and with over 360 years of history, MUFG has a global network with around 3,000 offices in more than 50 markets. The Group has over 180,000 employees, and offers services including commercial banking, trust banking, securities, credit cards, consumer finance, asset management, and leasing.

As one of the top financial groups globally with a vision to be the world's most trusted, we want to attract, nurture and retain the most talented individuals in the market. The size and range of MUFG's global business creates opportunities for our employees to stretch themselves and reap the rewards, whilst our common values, to behave with integrity and responsibility, and to build a culture which is fair, transparent, and honest, underpin everything that we do. We aim to be the financial partner of choice for our clients, whatever their requirements, building long-term relationships, serving society, and fostering shared and sustainable growth for a better world.

The EMEA LF Transaction Execution team sits within the EMEA Leveraged Finance and Mid Market Direct Lending team, which is part of the Global Corporate and Investment Banking Division of MUFG. The team works seamlessly with the Origination and Leveraged Capital Markets teams to bridge commercial expertise and deliver commercial structuring, advisory and execution services on sponsor leveraged finance loan transactions. The team also engages on each transaction with the in-house EMEA Legal team (responsible for engagement and management of external counsel for the transaction, management of the legal risks, legal negotiations and overall having oversight of the transactions from a legal perspective).

Please visit our website for more information - mufgemea.com.

NUMBER OF DIRECT REPORTS
None.
MAIN PURPOSE OF THE ROLE
We are seeking a Vice President with a transactional background in leveraged finance to join the front office EMEA Leveraged Finance (large cap and mid market) team in London.

This role is focused on (i) managing the commercial negotiation of transactional documentation for leveraged loan financing transactions (including mandate/commitment documents, facility agreements and intercreditor agreements (as applicable)); and (ii) assisting with any commercial structuring considerations and identifying any commercial risks or issues that arise in the broader transaction documentation or process.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Responsible for:
- Providing transaction execution support throughout the entire lifecycle of EMEA sponsor leveraged finance loan transactions, from origination (e.g. advice on grids/term sheets from a commercial structuring perspective, lead commercial negotiations of commitment / long form documentation) to closing/post-closing (e.g. funding, A&Es, add-ons)
- Leading commercial negotiation of financing documentation with sponsor clients, in conjunction with the in-house EMEA Legal team, which engages and manages external counsel
- Advising on the commercial aspects of the structuring of leveraged finance transactions
- In conjunction with the in-house EMEA Legal team, demonstrating an in-depth knowledge of different finance structures (e.g. TLB underwrite, direct lending), guarantee, security, subordination and leakage issues
- Reviewing commercial aspects of the documentation at term sheet and credit agreement stages for compliance with MUFG’s internal policies and best practice standards, in conjunction with the in-house EMEA Legal team
- Ensuring consistency regarding documentation commercial standards; being the central touch point/centre of excellence for emerging market trends and documentation-related internal escalation processes
- Coordinating the documentation process and ensuring that all relevant internal policy issues are addressed and required internal processes are obtained in time
- Keeping up to date with recent market trends in leveraged finance transactions
- Working closely with the in-house EMEA Legal team (who is responsible for identifying legal and documentation risks) with a view to continuously improve the control architecture around documentation
- Developing junior front-office staff and conducting internal training sessions for front-office on documentation commercial issues, market trends and  best practices in executing transactions

SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE
Work experience
- Significant and up to date market experience and knowledge of European and US cross-border leveraged finance transactions
- Experience in an in-house environment, either as a secondee or transaction execution role helpful
- Knowledge of high yield bond processes helpful.

Functional / Technical Skills and Competencies:
- Critical and creative thinker with strong business centricity
- Ability to work in a fast paced and pressured environment
- Ability to be proactive and anticipate issues with transaction documentation
- Simplifying the complex and ability to communicate clearly and succinctly
- Ability to take prudent risk based decisions, and balance the need for timely decisions in a pressured and market driven environment
- Skilled at building trusting relationships with internal stakeholders, senior management and external clients
- Confidence to function independently whilst proficient at recognising the need for escalation and specialist advice on highly complex issues, unusual situations and matters that may pose significant financial, reputational and/or other risk to MUFG
- Coaching mindset and aptitude for disseminating accumulated knowledge and experience among colleagues
- Innovative attitude focused on simplification and efficiencies (e.g. awareness and willingness to develop AI or streamline processes)

jobs.description:

MUFG Bank is seeking a Vice President, Non-Financial Risk Management (“NFRM”) to join the Global Corporate and Investment Banking (GCIB) APAC Business Risk Management team in Singapore.  The role will support the implementation and ongoing execution of GCIB APAC NFR Target Operating Model, with a particular focus on providing review and challenge of business risk assessments, issues and incident management, remediation oversight, thematic review and strategic initiatives across the region.   This position is ideal for someone who thrives in a collaborative environment and values transparency, early escalation, and continuous improvement. You will be joining a globally respected financial institution renowned for its commitment to integrity, strong governance, and nurturing a risk-aware culture. As part of MUFG’s APAC team, you will work closely with senior business partners and risk stakeholders across the region, helping to strengthen NFRM through effective oversight, challenge and consistent risk management practices.   The company fosters an inclusive workplace where your expertise will be valued and your professional growth supported through generous training opportunities and supportive leadership.

·         Join MUFG Bank’s APAC team in Singapore and play a key role in strengthening risk visibility, governance and consistent NFRM practices across the region.
·         Work in an environment that promotes transparency, early escalation, and continuous improvement, collaborating across the lines of defence to strengthen risk awareness, governance and effective remediation.
·         Benefit from supportive leadership, generous training opportunities, and a culture that values integrity, teamwork, and professional development.

What you'll do:
As Vice President, Non-Financial Risk Management at MUFG Bank, you will work closely with business functions, in-country NFRM teams, and risk stakeholders across GCIB APAC to strengthen the oversight and management of non-financial risks.  You will provide review and challenge of Line 1 risk assessments, risk ownership and the issue management cycle, including issue descriptions, root-cause analysis, the appropriateness of remediation plans and closure packages.  You will monitor material issues, incidents, breaches and remediation activities across the region, supporting timely escalation and regional visibility of key risk matters.  A key part of the role will be identifying recurring risk themes and emerging risks, supporting strategic projects and thematic reviews where broader NFR concerns emerge, and translating lessons learned into practical improvements. You will also work across the lines of defence to strengthen governance, clarify roles and responsibilities, and promote greater consistency, transparency and early risk escalation across the region.

- Provide review and challenge of Line 1 risk assessments, risk and control ownership, supporting consistent and effective NFRM across GCIB APAC.
- Drive greater consistency in  issues and incidents management across the region, work closely with  the business functions, in-country NFRM teams and  risk stakeholders.
- Facilitate discussions across regional business, NFRM and risk stakeholders to align on material risk matters, clarify ownership and actions, and drive timely resolution and escalation where required.
- Provide review and challenge throughout the issue management lifecycle, including reviewing issue descriptions, root cause analysis, action plans, completion timelines and closure packages.
- Develop meaningful management information and risk insights for senior leadership, covering material issues, incidents, remediation progress, emerging risks and recurring themes.
- Maintain regional visibility over material issues, incidents, breaches, remediation activities relevant to GCIB APAC, supporting timely escalation and regional visibility of key risk matters.
- Engage proactively with business management, in-country NFRM teams Second Lines of Defence and Internal Audit  to promote clear risk ownership, effective challenge and appropriate remediation. Identify recurring risk themes, control weaknesses and emerging risks, assessing potential risk implications across GCIB APAC markets.
- Design and implement effective findings governance by developing clear roles and responsibilities across remediation validation teams, business unit risk teams, and findings owners.
- Establish robust routines and procedures to ensure organisation-wide awareness, ownership, and execution of open findings and control gaps.
- Coordinate thematic reviews or targeted deep dives where issues, incidents or control weaknesses suggest broader non-financial risk concerns across GCIB APAC markets.
- Support strategic projects and initiatives involving material or emerging NFR considerations.
- Drive NFRM capability building through targeted training and knowledge-sharing, while identifying opportunities for process enhancement, simplification and automation across the region.

What you bring:
To excel as Vice President in Non-Financial Risk Management at MUFG Bank, you will bring extensive experience gained from internal audit, control assurance, issue management or operational risk roles, ideally within financial institutions or highly regulated environments such as 'Big 4' audit firms. Your background should include reviewing audit findings, analysing control gaps, investigating root causes, planning remediations, documenting closure evidence & driving thematic reviews or uplift initiatives. Deep familiarity with issue management lifecycles, incidents breaches, control testing outputs, RCSA findings & remediation tracking is essential. Strong project management skills are required enabling you to manage multiple priorities concurrently while solving problems pragmatically & collaboratively. Effective communication is vital—you must engage confidently with business units, country/regional teams & risk stakeholders promoting transparency early escalation & continuous improvement. Constructive challenge skills regarding root cause ownership, remediation quality & closure evidence verification will set you apart. Experience coordinating targeted reviews where recurring issues suggest broader NFR concerns is highly valued. Professional certifications in risk, audit, compliance or controls are advantageous but not mandatory.

·         Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience in Business, Finance, Operations, Risk Management, Audit or a related field.
·         Minimum 7 years’ experience in internal audit, risk and control management, compliance, issue management lifecycle oversight or operational risk roles within financial institutions or highly regulated environments such as 'Big 4' audit firms.
·         Prior exposure to reviewing audit findings, control gaps analysis, incident root cause investigations as well as remediation planning and closure evidence documentation.
·         Demonstrated ability to drive thematic reviews or remediation programmes including lessons learned initiatives or control uplift projects within corporate banking or investment banking operations.
·         Deep knowledge of issue management processes including incidents tracking, breaches analysis, control testing outputs interpretation (RCSA findings), remediation tracking methodologies.
·         Strong project management skills enabling prioritisation of multiple concurrent priorities; includes pragmatic problem-solving abilities within complex stakeholder environments.
·         Effective communication skills allowing engagement with business units at country/regional level as well as risk stakeholders; able to promote transparency & early escalation.
·         Constructive challenge capabilities regarding root cause analysis ownership assignment remediation quality evaluation & closure evidence verification.
·         Experience coordinating targeted reviews where incidents/issues/control weaknesses suggest broader concerns; able to scope & coordinate deep dives effectively.
·         Professional certifications in risk/audit/compliance/controls are beneficial but not mandatory; relevant internal training also acceptable.

What sets this company apart:
MUFG Bank stands out as one of the world’s leading financial institutions with a rich heritage rooted in trustworthiness, reliability, and commitment to customer success. The Singapore Branch forms an integral part of its global network offering employees exposure to international best practices while fostering a culture built on collaboration and inclusivity. At MUFG Bank you will find supportive leadership that encourages professional growth through ongoing training opportunities designed to keep your skills current amidst changing market dynamics. By joining MUFG Bank you become part of an institution that prioritises ethical conduct, compliance excellence, and genuine care for its people, making it an employer of choice within the financial sector.

This includes the effective identification, assessment, monitoring, and mitigation of operational and non-financial risks across a diverse portfolio of corporate and investment banking products and services.

The successful candidate will partner closely with business, product, operations, compliance, and risk management stakeholders to help strengthen the overall risk and control environment. This individual will contribute to the execution of the business unit's risk management framework, ensuring risks are proactively identified, appropriately assessed, and effectively controlled in alignment with regulatory expectations and organizational risk appetite.

Responsibilities

- Serve as a trusted advisor to business and risk leadership on RCSA program standards, risk governance, control effectiveness, emerging risks, and regulatory expectations, providing credible review and challenge and recommendations where required.

- Leverage and apply knowledge of regulations by embedding its impact and applicability in the RCSA through execution of the compliance engagement model.
- Develop and present clear, decision-oriented risk and control reporting for senior management and governance committees, including material exposures, control weaknesses, residual-risk concerns, emerging risks, overdue actions, and matters requiring escalation.
- Establish continuous monitoring metrics, to provide meaningful insight into risk exposure, monitor key risk indicators, key control indicators, thresholds, and other risk metrics to identify changes in risk exposure, control performance, loss events, and issue-remediation status; escalate breaches and adverse trends in accordance with governance requirements.
- Partner with and support GCIB teams with ad hoc requests for information and real-time risk management inquiries.
- Act as a subject matter expert for GCIB when collaborating with cross-functional stakeholders, including Compliance, Legal, Operational Risk, Audit, Technology, and Operations teams, to strengthen the overall control environment.
- Coach junior team members and contributing to team capability development
- Identify opportunities to use approved automation, analytics, and artificial-intelligence tools to improve the efficiency, consistency, and quality of RCSA activities, in accordance with applicable information-security, data-privacy, records-management, and technology-risk requirements.

Qualifications

- 7+ years of experience in risk management, operational risk, controls, audit, corporate and investment banking, or a related financial services function.

- Strong understanding of banking products, operational risk frameworks, and control management principles.

- Strong experience with RCSA process documentation, risk and control assessments, and operational risk frameworks.

- Excellent skills in risk assessment analysis, governance, and reporting; solid understanding of business and financial markets.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present technical information effectively to diverse audiences.

- Ability to analyze risk trends and identify indicators of changing risk levels.

- Senior stakeholder management experience and ability to establish rapport, credibility, trust, and respect throughout the organization.

- Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, highly regulated environment.

- Strong attention to detail, organizational skills, and commitment to delivering high-quality work.

- Ability to work effectively both independently and in collaborative environments.

- Proficiency with risk and control platforms, data visualization, and analytical tools; experience with platforms such as OpenPages, Archer, Power BI, Tableau, or comparable systems is preferred.

We stand for our values, building long-term relationships, serving society, and fostering shared and sustainable growth for a better world.

With a vision to be the world’s most trusted financial group, it’s part of our culture to put people first, listen to new and diverse ideas and collaborate toward greater innovation, speed and agility. This means investing in talent, technologies, and tools that empower you to own your career.

Join MUFG, where being inspired is expected and making a meaningful impact is rewarded.

The selected colleague will work at an MUFG office or client sites four days per week and work remotely one day. A member of our recruitment team will provide more details.

Job Summary: This role is a member of the CISO of the Americas team within an embedded Cybersecurity GRC function. The AVP will support governance of the cyber risk lifecycle by monitoring execution across contributing teams, tracking status and gaps, and ensuring lifecycle records and outcomes are complete, consistent, and traceable. The role will also support the Cyber Risk Institute (CRI) Profile maturity program by coordinating with control owners, tracking assessment progress and outcomes, maintaining the maturity tracker, and preparing maturity reporting. This role is well suited to an organized, detail-oriented cyber risk professional who is comfortable working across technical and business teams.
Primary Responsibilities:
Cyber Risk Lifecycle Governance
- Coordinate lifecycle activities across contributing teams, tracking status, handoffs, approvals, and open items through to closure.
- Review lifecycle outcomes for completeness, consistency, and traceability, and follow up with responsible teams on gaps or delays.
- Escalate missed milestones, unresolved dependencies, and process issues to management with clear context and recommended next steps.
- Maintain process documentation, RACI, and procedures.

CRI Profile Maturity Support
- Coordinate with control owners to track completion of CRI Profile maturity assessments against program timelines.
- Review assessment outcomes and maturity ratings for consistency across the program, and flag gaps or open items for management review.
- Escalate overdue submissions, unresolved maturity gaps, and remediation delays to management.
- Maintain the maturity tracker and remediation status, and prepare draft reporting and supporting materials for reporting submissions.

Reporting and Metrics
- Compile KRI/KPI data and prepare recurring status and governance reporting for GRC leadership, highlighting trends, risks, and items requiring decision or escalation.

Audit and Regulatory Support
- Support responses to internal audit, second line, regulatory, and other requests by coordinating with responsible teams, tracking requests to completion, and organizing the response.

Stakeholder Coordination
- Serve as a working-level point of contact for business, system, and control owners and contributing cyber teams, explaining requirements in clear terms and following up on deliverables.

Process Improvement
- Identify opportunities to streamline manual coordination, tracking, and reporting tasks, and support enhancements to GRC tooling.

Qualifications:
- Experience: 4-7 years' experience in cyber risk, IT risk, GRC, or information security. Working knowledge of core cybersecurity domains such as Identity Access Management, Data Security, Configuration Management, Logging, Incident Response, and Secure Software Development Lifecycle, sufficient to understand control outcomes and risk information. Prior audit, assurance, or advisory experience (e.g., Big 4 cyber risk advisory, internal audit, or IT audit) a plus.
- Cloud Security: Working knowledge of cloud security concepts across major cloud service providers.
- Documentation: Experience writing process documentation and maintaining traceable, audit-ready records.
- Regulatory Knowledge: Familiarity with frameworks and regulations relevant to cyber risk in banking, such as NIST CSF 2.0, the CRI Profile, NIST SP 800-53, the FFIEC IT Handbook, NYDFS Part 500, and Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) and Federal Reserve Board (FRB) expectations or other frameworks such as Payment Card Industry (PCI). Experience supporting regulatory examinations, matters requiring attention (MRAs), or consent orders within a large financial institution is preferred.
- Framework Maturity Assessments (Preferred): Experience supporting framework-based maturity assessments such as the CRI Profile or NIST CSF.
- Certifications (Preferred): One or more of CRISC, CISA, or CompTIA Security+.
- Collaboration: Ability to constructively work both independently and in collaborative environments involving all levels of management and employees.
- Multitasking: Ability to manage multiple priorities concurrently, prioritize, and efficiently complete responsibilities while maintaining the highest quality.
- GRC Tools (Preferred): Experience with GRC platforms and workflow tools.
- Skills: Excellent analytical, organizational, and conceptual skills. Excellent oral and written communication skills.

Education & Certifications:
- Bachelor's degree in Information Security or a closely related discipline, or equivalent related experience.
